full_judgment:
A.T.M. Afzal, CJ: This appeal, by leave at the instance of the informant appellant, is from a judgment and order dated 13 August, 1998 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case. No. 3529 of 1998 allowing an application under section 526 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the accused-respondents and transferring Sessions Case No. 633 of 1996 under section 302/149 of the Penal Code from the 3rd Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka to the Court of Sessions Judge, Narsingdi for trial. 

 2. For the purpose of disposal of this appeal it will be sufficient to notice that the accused respondents and one Faruk Thakur (absconding on jumping the bail) are being tried for the murder of one Shamsul Alam in the Gulshan Residential Area on 7.1.96 in the aforesaid Sessions Case. 14 prosecution witnesses have already been examined and because of pre-occupation of the learned Sessions Judge who was holding the trial, he transferred the case to the Third Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka after rejecting an application for transfer of the case filed by the accused. The learned Additional Sessions Judge on receipt of the case record on 19.3.98 cancelled the bail of the accused persons and took them into custody upon finding that they had resorted to tactics to delay the conclusion of the trial. 

 3. The accused then moved the High Court Division for transfer of the case from the said court "to any other Court or any other Sessions Division around Dhaka or to any other court of competent jurisdiction in this Sessions Division." 

 4. The High Court Division in a lengthy judgment which appeared to us to be intolerably verbose found only two facts for consideration to see "whether there is any basis or foundation for the apprehension on the part of the accused-petitioners that they may not get fair and impartial trial in the court where the case is pending and whether to secure the ends of justice the case is required to be transferred". It was noticed that the accused persons except the aforesaid Faruk Thakur (who was absconding) were granted bail by the learned Sessions Judge on different dates but on 8.2.98 the learned Sessions Judge cancelled the bail of all the accused persons on the ground that they had misused the privilege of bail granted to them and created obstruction in the trial. On that date most of the accused were present but adjournment was prayed for on behalf of two other accused on the ground of illness in one case and in another the accused being in custody in connection with another criminal case. On 12.2.98 the two absentee accused surrendered and prayer for bail was made on their behalf but the learned Sessions Judge rejected their prayer. Subsequently, however, they were granted bail. 

 5. On 5.3.98 an application was presented before the Sessions Judge for transfer of the case to another Court of competent jurisdiction under his Sessions Division. The application was heard on 19.3.98 and the same was rejected. But the learned Sessions Judge because of his own pre-occupation transferred the case to the 3rd Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka. As already noticed, the learned Additional Sessions Judge on receipt of the case record took the accused in custody after cancelling their bail. The High Court Division upon a consideration of the aforesaid facts held that those facts "undoubtedly lead a suggestion that the apprehension in the mind of the accused petitioners that they will not get fair and impartial trial and treatment in the hands of the Additional Sessions Judge or any other Judge of the Sessions Division of Dhaka got a basis and the apprehension cannot be ruled out". 

 7. The grounds upon which the High Court Division may make an order of transfer of a case from one Court to another are enumerated in section 526 Cr. P.C. They have been elaborately noticed in the impugned judgment. The ground for transfer in the present case was the apprehension of the accused that a fair and impartial trial cannot be had in the 3rd Court of Additional Sessions Judge. It is an elementary principle that a mere apprehension in the mind of the accused is not sufficient for asking for an order of transfer. The party seeking transfer must furnish facts and grounds upon which such apprehension is entertained and it will be for the High Court Division to judge whether the allegations appeared to be such that a fair and impartial trial in a particular Court cannot be had. The only fact disclosed in the present case is that in the midst of the trial the accused persons were taken into custody once by the learned Sessions Judge and on transfer of the case to his court by the learned Additional Sessions Judge on the ground that they were causing obstruction to the conclusion of the trial by remaining on bail. For example, on 8.2.98 because of the absence of two of the accused prayer for adjournment was made although the other accused were present. The learned Sessions Judge, inter alia, on the ground hat they were creating obstruction in the trial. On transfer to the 3rd Court of Additional Sessions Judge on 19.3.98 the accused were present but none of their Senior Advocates appeared and only a junior Advocate was present. The accused were again taken into custody on the ground that they adopted dilatory tactics to avoid conclusions of the trial. From these facts, the High Court Division held that there was a bias for apprehension in the mind of the accused that a fair and impartial trial in the Court of the Additional Sessions cannot be had and that "the apprehension cannot be ruled out." 

 8. It must be said that the High Court Division was entirely wrong in reading a basis for apprehension in the mind of the accused about fair trial from the mere fact that during trial their bails was cancelled by the courts concerned only to ensure a speedy conclusion of the trial. It has been noticed that the bail was cancelled exactly for the said purpose as the trial was being dragged on for certain lapses on the part of the accused who were on bail on different dates. It is not unusual that the accused persons who remain on bail are taken into custody during trial for holding a quick trial without unforeseen interruptions. The taking of custody of the accused in the midst of the trial was therefore neither unusual nor such a thing as would suggest bias or preconceivedness in the mind of the court against the accused. The High Court Division ought to have been aware of this ordinary procedure adopted in the trial of Sessions cases. If such ground as was considered sufficient for apprehension in the mind of the accused in the present case is to be upheld then the High Court Division will be flooded with transfer applications. However, we have already found that the mere fact of taking into custody of the accused during trial can never be a basis for making a prayer for transfer of the case unless there is other convincing and reasonable grounds for apprehension in the mind of the accused. Further we have found no sense at all in the impugned order transferring the case to the Sessions Division at Narsingdi when the accused themselves had prayed a tenatively for transfer of the case to any other competent court of the same Sessions Division, namely, Dhaka. It was a totally unreasonable order as it did not take into consideration the difficulties of the prosecution to take their witnesses to Narsingdi for trial. We are sorry to notice that some irresponsible law officers of the Attorney General apparently without any instructions from the prosecution agreed to the transfer of the case to Narsingdi. The learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the State before us has disowned the agreement made by the State lawyers in the High Court Division and supported the appellant for setting aside the impugned judgment of the High Court Division which, he submitted, was wholly illegal and unreasonable. The High Court Division we are sorry to say, has failed to appreciate the spirit and purpose of a transfer and the requirements for the purpose of holding that the apprehension expressed by the accused appeared to be probable and reasonable. The order transferring the case to Narsingdi was entirely bad because the accused themselves had alternatively prayer for transfer to any other competent Court at Dhaka.
